newsitem.title: UK: SNOOKER-DOHERTY WINS LAST TO STAY LEVEL.
newsitem.headline: SNOOKER-DOHERTY WINS LAST TO STAY LEVEL.

text.p: Irishman Ken Doherty compiled his highest break of the session, a 75 in the final frame, to draw level at 4-4 with Alain Robidoux of Canada as their world snooker semifinal began on Thursday.
It was a close session all the way with never more than one frame separating the two.
Doherty, the seventh seed who beat six-times champion Steve Davis and second seed John Higgins in his previous two matches, took the first frame with a break of 66.
Robidoux, seeded 14th, replied with a break of 55 to win the second then after Doherty missed two easy reds in the third, Robidoux fluked a crucial yellow to lead 2-1.
Back came the 27-year-old Irishman in the fourth with a break of 60 as he won the frame 99-0.

The Canadian, a 36-year-old from Montreal, took the lead again with breaks of 69 and 62 as he won the fifth 131-0 but Doherty won a scrappy sixth frame 62-26 despite potting a red as he sank the blue.
Once more, Robidoux went in front, winning another erratic frame 67-23 before Doherty came good in the last to draw level for the third time.
The pair, who resume on Friday, are battling it out over the best-of-33 frames to become the first non-British world championship finalist since Robidoux's compatriot Cliff Thorburn in 1983.
World champion Steven Hendry of Scotland and Thailand's James Wattana were beinnning the second semifinal later on Thursday.
